candidates.attacker_control: Any remote network client that can open a TCP connection to the monitor port (default 5001, bound to the wildcard address by `new ServerSocket(port)`) controls the entire byte stream. The bytes are handed directly to `new ObjectInputStream(socket.getInputStream())` and `in.readObject()`; no authentication, no source restriction, no TLS, no serialization filter or class allow-list is applied to the stream.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Searched the repository for ObjectInputFilter / ValidatingObjectInputStream / resolveClass-based filtering: none protect this stream (the only resolveClass is in the unrelated class-file parser axis-rt-core/.../utils/bytecode/ClassReader.java). Checked the documentation/resources: src/site/xdoc/user-guide.xml:1309 and install.xml:438 plus axis-war/src/main/resources/i18n.properties:51 state the SOAP monitor is NOT enabled by default for security reasons, which contradicts the actual deployment descriptor and strengthens rather than weakens the finding. Checked other readObject sinks: samples (bidbuy RegistryService, TestRef) and the monitor client/applet deserialize local files or server responses, not server-side request data. Checked AdminServlet/Admin deployment path: its mapping is commented out in web.xml and commands only work when isDevelopment() is true. Checked XXE handling: XMLUtils installs DefaultEntityResolver on SAX parsers. Checked trust-all socket factory: SunFakeTrustSocketFactory is an explicitly selected opt-in attribute, not default.
candidates.impact: Unauthenticated network-side Java deserialization inside the servlet container JVM. With a suitable gadget chain on the classpath this is remote code execution; independent of gadgets it allows construction of arbitrary object graphs, class resolution/instantiation from the application classpath, and denial of service (e.g., resource-exhausting object graphs or errors aborted per connection). Any connected client also receives all monitored SOAP traffic broadcast by publishMessage, exposing message content that may include credentials or tokens.
candidates.prerequisites: The Axis WAR (axis-war/axis.war) or any equivalent deployment that includes axis-rt-soapmonitor and registers SOAPMonitorService must be running, and the monitor port must be reachable from the attacker. For code-execution impact, a usable Java deserialization gadget chain must exist on the container classpath; without one, attacker-controlled object graph instantiation and resource-exhaustion/DoS are still possible. The Axis WAR does not enable admin services by default, but it does register this servlet with load-on-startup and port 5001.
candidates.root_cause: The SOAP Monitor runtime accepts raw Java serialization streams from any TCP client and deserializes them without authentication, allow-listing or any ObjectInputFilter, and the Axis WAR deployment descriptor enables the listener at webapp startup (load-on-startup 100, port 5001), even though the product docs and i18n resources state the monitor is disabled by default.
candidates.title: Unauthenticated Java deserialization in SOAP Monitor service, enabled at startup by axis.war
candidates.trace: web.xml registers SOAPMonitorService with init-param SOAPMonitorPort=5001 and load-on-startup 100 (lines 34-45) and maps it to /SOAPMonitor (lines 62-65); axis-war/pom.xml includes axis-rt-soapmonitor (lines 45-49). At startup SOAPMonitorService.init() reads the port and executes `server_socket = new ServerSocket(Integer.parseInt(port))`, then starts ServerSocketThread (lines 98-117). ServerSocketThread.run() calls `server_socket.accept()` for any peer and spawns `new ConnectionThread(socket)` (lines 181-189). ConnectionThread's constructor creates `in = new ObjectInputStream(socket.getInputStream())` (lines 214-216) and its run() loops on `Object o = in.readObject();` (lines 237-242) until the stream closes. The same unauthenticated ConnectionThread instances are appended to the shared `connections` vector, to which SOAPMonitorHandler.publishMessage broadcasts monitored SOAP request/response content.
candidates.unverified: No code was built, deployed or executed; the finding is static. RCE severity depends on whether a usable gadget chain is present in a given deployment classpath (not established here). The exact released binary artifact could differ from this source snapshot, and no version-control history was available to confirm which configuration is intended for release. Line numbers reference the reviewed snapshot only.

coverage_summary: Reviewed the 1227-file snapshot (no files excluded by the scope filters). Examined module layout and poms (root pom.xml modules, axis-war, axis-rt-core, axis-rt-soapmonitor), the Axis WAR deployment descriptor and JSPs, the SOAP Monitor runtime/handler/constants, key transport and utility classes (AxisServlet, AdminServlet, SimpleAxisServer-related code, XMLUtils, JSSESocketFactory, SunFakeTrustSocketFactory, SessionUtils, AttachmentPart/ManagedMemoryDataSource, JavaUtils), plus documentation under src/site/xdoc. Ran targeted text searches for ObjectInputStream/readObject, XMLDecoder, ObjectInputFilter, resolveClass, Runtime.exec/ProcessBuilder, ScriptEngine, DocumentBuilderFactory/setFeature, Class.forName/newInstance, servlet request.getParameter, and trust-manager code. The analysis is static; nothing was compiled, deployed or executed.
limitations: Static source review only; no build, deployment, scanner or runtime confirmation was performed, so the candidate remains a lead, not a confirmed vulnerability.
RCE impact depends on a gadget chain being present on an actual deployment classpath; that environment condition was not verified.
No version-control history or released-artifact comparison was available, so it was not possible to confirm which web.xml configuration is intended for the next release.
Codegen, tests, integration, interop-mock, tcpmon, samples and other auxiliary modules were inspected only selectively via directory listings and targeted searches, not read exhaustively.
Default port binding behavior is inferred from `new ServerSocket(port)` semantics (wildcard bind); no runtime check of the deployed listener was possible.

rejected_leads.lead: Dynamic query-string handler loading in AxisServlet (Class.forName followed by Method.invoke)
rejected_leads.reason: The class name comes from server-side transport configuration (qs.* options), not from the HTTP request; the query string only selects among configured handler names, so it is not attacker-controlled code loading.

The admin servlet's URL mapping is commented out by default in axis-war/web.xml and its state-changing commands only run when the server is in development mode; it is not exposed in the default configuration.
XMLUtils.getSAXParser installs DefaultEntityResolver, and no clearly reachable unmitigated parser path was confirmed; lower evidence than the deserialization sink.

rejected_leads.lead: Client-side deserialization in soapmonitor-client and the SOAP Monitor applet (SOAPMonitor.java:1418-1421, SOAPMonitorApplet.java:435-456)
rejected_leads.reason: These read objects sent by the monitor server (reverse direction, requires a malicious/compromised server); the server-side network deserialization is the stronger and more directly reachable issue.

rejected_leads.lead: Unauthenticated broadcast of monitored SOAP messages via SOAPMonitorService.publishMessage / SOAPMonitorHandler
rejected_leads.reason: Same service and same missing-authentication root cause as the deserialization issue; treated as an additional impact rather than a separate candidate to avoid splitting one root cause.

rejected_leads.lead: Trust-all TLS behavior in SunFakeTrustSocketFactory / FakeX509TrustManager
rejected_leads.reason: It is an explicitly chosen opt-in socket factory (hook for accepting unsigned server certificates), not enabled by default; no attacker-controlled configuration path was confirmed.

rejected_leads.lead: Sample-code ObjectInputStream usage (samples/bidbuy RegistryService.java:29, samples/attachments TestRef.java:255)
rejected_leads.reason: Sample applications, not part of the deployable Axis runtime; local-file or server-response data only.

summary: Apache Axis 1.4.1-SNAPSHOT source snapshot (1227 readable files). The strongest source-evidenced issue is an unauthenticated, enabled-by-default Java deserialization endpoint in the SOAP Monitor service: `SOAPMonitorService` opens a TCP server socket at servlet startup and calls `ObjectInputStream.readObject()` on whatever any client sends, with no authentication and no class filtering, while the Axis WAR deployment descriptor still registers the servlet with `load-on-startup` and the documented default port 5001. The service's own docs/i18n claim it is disabled by default, which makes the enabled configuration the concrete defect. Other leads (AdminServlet, XXE handling, trust-all socket factory, client-side monitor deserialization, dynamic query-handler loading) were examined and do not reach the same evidence/impact level.
